title: m00a: make the skeleton enforceable - a gate that can fail, and a second key
body:
Closes the M00a foundation milestone (`SPEC/00a-foundation.md`).

The starter shipped every contract and almost no enforcement. `pave gate decide`
was a stub that printed and exited 0, `make check` ran pytest against zero tests
and swallowed the exit code, and CODEOWNERS routed to teams that do not resolve.
Every green check mark in the first commit was vacuous. This milestone makes the
skeleton enforceable, so that every number recorded from M00b onward means
something.

## What lands

- **A gate that can fail.** `pave gate decide` validates verdict records and
  blocks on `FAIL` (exit 1, pages the service team) or on missing / unparseable /
  schema-invalid / `fail_closed: false` / `INFRA` (exit 2, pages the platform).
  Absence blocks — a step that crashes before writing its verdict cannot read as
  "nothing to report, therefore fine" (G2).
- **G9 enforced rather than asserted.** GitHub never lets a PR's author approve
  their own PR, so with one operator the two-key second key was unobtainable, not
  merely inconvenient. `pave gate two-key` collects it as a checked attestation
  with a mandatory written rationale instead (ADR-013). **This PR is the first
  thing it ran against, and it blocked it** — see "Seat review" below.
- **80 hermetic tests** where there were 0.
- **The golden set at 25 cases**, authored before the control has ever run.
- The artifacts the committed contracts already referenced but did not have:
  six tool schemas, the agent answer schema, the judge rubric, the ADV-002
  poisoned-catalog fixture.
- ADR-003, 004, 007, 009 (all cited but never written), ADR-012, ADR-013.
  ADR-001 amended, not superseded.

## Two things the repo was claiming that were not true

**M07's demo shipped pre-placed at commit one.** `disclosure-004` was already in
`cases.yaml` tagged with the rule meant to produce it, and `MER-AI-0001` was
already `status: enforced` pointing at that case. Claim 6 is "a rule delta
disposed end-to-end into eval cases" — unprovable when both halves are already
there. Both moved to M07; a contract test blocks reintroducing the pre-placement.

**`branch-protection.md` documented an unachievable setup**, calling teams-of-one
plus "Require review from Code Owners" the thing that "makes seats real." It is
satisfiable on zero PRs. Rewritten to the achievable configuration, with an
honest table of which invariants are machine-enforced (G2, G7, G8, G9) and which
remain conventions under one operator (G6).

## Advances no claim directly

M00a makes claims 2 and 5 enforceable rather than proving either. The proof
artifacts belong to M04.

## Seat review

The first run of `two-key` **blocked this PR**. Its base is the initial commit,
so the diff *adds* `platform/registry/tools.yaml`, `quality/adversarial/probes.yaml`,
and the verdict and history schemas to version control — unmodified in content,
but added — and the original body declared only two of the five seats. It also
demanded an ADR for the probe corpus, which surfaced that ADR-009 was owed: this
PR fixes the golden set at 25, which is ADR-009's decision, and the row had been
sitting in the table unwritten. Both are now correct. The mechanism found a real
gap on its first run.

Two-Key-Disposition: ai-quality
Two-Key-Disposition: platform-eng
Two-Key-Disposition: tool-owner
Two-Key-Disposition: legal-sp
Two-Key-Disposition: security
ADR: docs/adr/ADR-009-corpus-sizes.md
Two-Key-Rationale: the golden set grows from 4 to 25 and the judge rubric is
  added as documentation only, not yet scored (ADR-012 defers the judge to M03,
  so no threshold moves here); the gate criteria change is the gate gaining the
  ability to fail at all, which tightens rather than loosens; the two-key rules
  are introduced by this PR, so it attests to its own mechanism under the rule
  it establishes; and `tools.yaml` and `probes.yaml` enter version control with
  their starter content byte-for-byte unchanged — no consequence class is
  raised and no probe is downgraded, which ADR-009 and the contract tests now
  both pin.

title: adr-014: denominate eval budgets in tokens, not dollars (+ adr-015: the regional pin)
body:
Two-Key-Disposition: ai-quality
Two-Key-Rationale: The 25 golden budget ceilings were denominated in Anthropic
  first-party rates while this project bills through Bedrock, so every one of
  them was wrong in a currency the project does not spend. Rather than re-derive
  the dollars, the assert moves to tokens: a dollar ceiling tracks a vendor price
  list that moves without a commit, so a Bedrock price change would re-score all
  25 cases and make m00b and m04 incomparable with nothing in the repo changing.
  Ceilings are derived from measurement against the pinned profile (input
  1163-1181, output 75-158 across six diverse cases), not tuned until a run
  passed, and nothing has been recorded yet. The author's four complexity tiers
  are preserved. Verdict and history schemas gain tokens_in/tokens_out because
  otherwise the new assert has nowhere to be recorded; cost_usd stays as the
  rendered report and its "blocks like quality regressions" description is
  corrected, since that would put a price list back into a merge decision.

Replaces #7, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted on
merge of #6. Same two commits, rebased onto `main`; no content changed.

## Why not just re-derive the dollars

That was the plan, and it was wrong. A dollar ceiling is not a property of the
system under test; it is a property of a price list that changes without a
commit. A Bedrock price cut between m00b and m04 would improve every score while
the platform stood still — the same "two definitions on one line" failure
ADR-012's consequences section warns about. The regional premium (ADR-015) and
cache pricing pile further multipliers on top.

So the blocking assert is tokens, and dollars are rendered at report time from a
pinned rate table where a price change is a visible diff in one file.

```yaml
- budget: { model: haiku, tokens_in: 1500, tokens_out: 300, p95_ms: 1800 }
```

**This also unblocks M00b.** Scoring no longer needs a Bedrock rate — which I
could not obtain from the AWS pricing page, the AWS Pricing API (catalog still
stops at Claude 3), or Anthropic's Bedrock docs. The rate is now needed only to
render a report, and its absence gates nothing.

## Where the numbers came from

Measured against `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, sending the
committed system prompt, answer schema, and `data/catalog.json` inlined — the
control's shape:

| Case | input | output |
|---|---|---|
| `concise-022` | 1168 | 124 |
| `blackout-001` | 1171 | 125 |
| `recommend-003` | 1172 | 75 |
| `multi-023` | 1181 | 151 |
| `headroom-026` | 1177 | 157 |
| `edge-025` | 1163 | 158 |

Input is near-constant — the prompt dominates it — so `tokens_in` is uniform at
1500. Output varies, so the author's four complexity tiers move there:
300/400/500/600, roughly twice the measured worst case per band. `p95_ms` is
untouched.

No value was tuned until the control passed. Nothing has been run and recorded
yet, which is the only reason editing these cases is legitimate at all.

## The finding that matters more than the numbers

| Shape | input tokens |
|---|---|
| Ungoverned — whole catalog inlined (M00b) | 1138 |
| Governed — one retrieved title (M02+) | 891 |
| Floor — no catalog | 754 |

Inlining the entire catalog costs **247 tokens**. At ADR-009's five-title,
1,173-byte corpus, "the whole catalog in every prompt" is nearly free.

`SPEC/00b-baseline.md` predicts *"Cost/latency — higher than budget on some
cases — whole catalog in every prompt."* **That hypothesis will not hold**, and
not because the control is well built. The control will pass the budget axis,
and that pass is **unearned** in exactly the sense SPEC/00b's honesty clause
defines. Better found now than in M00b's journal — the spec's hypothesis row
should be corrected at branch cut.

Token budgets still catch what they are for: prompt bloat, context-stuffing
regressions, runaway generation. Those are real at any corpus size.

## Also here

**ADR-015** records the `us.` pin as a decision. It carries a documented 10%
premium over `global.`, and PR #5 pinned it only because it was the profile that
happened to get verified first. Keeping it — a platform whose story is
classification-driven routing should not let inference land wherever capacity
is — but recorded, with BUILD.md noting costs must be priced at regional rates.

**Contract test** `test_no_budget_is_denominated_in_currency` fails on any
`cost_usd` reintroduced into a case, because a reintroduced value would look
plausible and re-couple the suite quietly.

## Verification

`pave check`: **266 tests**. Ruff clean across the repo. Verdict records
round-trip with the new token fields. `pave gate two-key` was confirmed to
**block** this diff with no disposition, naming all three rule classes, before
the disposition above was written.

## Found, not fixed here

`pave gate two-key` crashes on Windows when it has problems to report —
`render()` emits `✗` into a cp1252 console and raises `UnicodeEncodeError`
instead of printing the blocking reason. CI is unaffected (UTF-8), so it has
been invisible. It is the same class as M00a's BOM bug: a governance check that
fails for a reason that is not the team's fault. Not fixed here because
`pave/twokey.py` is itself a two-key path needing **platform-eng as well**, and
that fix should not ride inside an eval-threshold change.

title: pave: let the gate report why it blocked on a non-UTF-8 console
body:
`pave gate two-key` renders its blocking path with U+2717. A Windows console
running cp1252 cannot encode that character, so `print` raised
`UnicodeEncodeError` and the command **died before emitting the reason** — a
traceback and exit 1, with the blocking reason nowhere on screen.

Exit 1 is coincidentally the correct code. That is why this survived: the check
looked like it worked. CI never caught it because GitHub runners are UTF-8, and
M00a's Windows-parity DoD was written about `pave check`, not the gate commands.

This is the same class as M00a's BOM bug — a governance check failing for a
reason that is not the team's fault. Those are the failures that teach people to
route around a gate instead of fixing it.

## Why the boundary, and not just the glyph

The obvious fix is to swap `✗` for ASCII in `twokey.py`. I measured the
alternative instead of assuming. Auditing every non-ASCII character in `pave/`
found four:

| Character | Count | cp1252 | cp437 | ascii |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EM DASH | 50 | OK | **FAILS** | **FAILS** |
| MIDDLE DOT | 2 | OK | OK | **FAILS** |
| HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS | 1 | OK | **FAILS** | **FAILS** |
| BALLOT X | 1 | **FAILS** | **FAILS** | **FAILS** |

On cp1252 only the ballot X fails, which is why that is the crash we saw. **On
cp437 the fifty em dashes fail too** — so editing that one character would have
left the same command broken on a different codepage, and `two-key: SATISFIED —
every owning seat disposed` would crash just as hard.

Routing rendered output through a helper that degrades instead of raising covers
all four, keeps the real glyph on UTF-8 terminals and in CI logs, and protects
`gate decide` and `gate comment` as well. `_emit` reads stdout's encoding per
call rather than caching it, since it differs between a console, a pipe, and a
redirect to file.

## Before and after, same command, cp1252 console

Before — `UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '✗'`,
no output. After:

```
two-key: BLOCKED (G9)
  ? golden cases, eval thresholds, and headroom policy: changed
    services/highlights-agent/evals/golden/cases.yaml — missing disposition
    from ai-quality. Add `Two-Key-Disposition: <seat>` to the PR body.
```

The glyph degrades to `?`; the reason survives, which is the point.

## On the seat requirement

**This lands in `pave/cli.py`, not `pave/twokey.py`, so it needs no two-key
disposition** — `two-key: not required` on this diff.

Flagging that explicitly because it would be easy to read as routing around the
governance path. It is not the motive: the crash is at the `print`, the rule
logic is untouched, and the cp437 result above is what decided the layer. If you
would rather this be a `twokey.py` change carrying **ai-quality + platform-eng**,
say so and I will move it — but it would then fix strictly less.

## Tests

`pave/tests/test_console_encoding.py`, 7 cases. They parametrise cp1252, cp437,
ascii and utf-8 **explicitly** rather than relying on the host codepage, so a
Windows-only bug stays covered when the suite runs on a Linux runner — otherwise
this regression would be untestable in the only place it is currently tested.

They render through the real `twokey.render`, so a future glyph added there is
covered without anyone remembering to update the test. One test asserts the
glyph is preserved unchanged on UTF-8, pinning that this fix does not quietly
downgrade good output.

`pave check`: **279 tests**. Ruff clean.

title: M00b: the ungoverned baseline (the control)
body:
Two-Key-Disposition: ai-quality
Two-Key-Rationale: This records the project's first baselines — goldens 15/25
  and adversarial 0/10 — into the append-only history, which is a decision and
  not a cleanup. Recorded as-run against sha 515ee70, the commit the runs were
  actually produced against, and deliberately before any correction: three of the
  ten golden failures are latency-only against p95_ms ceilings that were never
  derived from measurement (measured 1182-2292ms against ceilings of 1800-2400),
  the same flaw ADR-014 fixed for cost and missed for latency. Those ceilings are
  NOT adjusted here. Nothing had been recorded yet, but the run has now been seen,
  and editing a case after seeing its result is the direction CLAUDE.md forbids
  outright. The tightening lands as its own PR after m00b is tagged, so the
  baseline is never retroactively improved. Four passes carry unearned marks with
  reasons, recorded into the entry itself rather than left in prose: the control
  claimed the entitlement-check tool it does not have in 10 of the 11 cases that
  assert provenance. The adversarial 0/10 is by construction and is the real
  score, not a harness limitation.

**Draft — this is the M00b milestone branch.** One milestone, one branch, one
tag at close (CLAUDE.md). It stays open and accumulates commits; opening it as a
draft now means every push gets `gate` and `two-key` rather than discovering at
close that something went red days earlier.

First commit is the spec amendment, deliberately landed **before any of M00b is
built**. `SPEC/00b-baseline.md` predates ADR-012, ADR-014 and ADR-015, and three
of its statements did not survive them. Each would have biased the control's
recorded numbers if found afterwards.

## What the amendment corrects

**Who builds the runner.** The spec never said. ADR-012 originally read as
though M00a would; M00a built none of it — correctly, because at M00a there was
nothing to score. The runner is M00b's, and it is now a DoD line rather than an
assumed dependency.

**Two numbers, not one.** Judge axes are `ADVISORY` and unscored here; M03
re-scores this same commit and appends with `supersedes`. The progression table
must footnote which number is which, or an M04 judged score gets compared
against an M00b unjudged one and a change in *what was measured* reads as
platform improvement.

**The cost hypothesis is wrong.** Measured before the control exists:

| Prompt shape | input tokens |
|---|---|
| Ungoverned — whole catalog inlined | 1138 |
| Governed — one retrieved title | 891 |
| Floor — no catalog | 754 |

Inlining the whole catalog costs 247 tokens. At ADR-009's five-title corpus that
is nearly free, so the control will sit inside budget and **that pass is
unearned** in the honesty clause's exact sense — the assertion cannot
meaningfully fail, and it passes for reasons unrelated to how the control is
built.

## The struck row

The hypothesis table keeps its original wording with the cost row struck
through, not deleted. A pre-registered prediction quietly edited to match what
its author later learned is worth nothing — and pre-registering it was precisely
to make this kind of correction auditable.

What changed is evidence, not hindsight: the measurement was taken against the
pinned model *before* the control was written, so the corrected claim is still a
prediction, only a better-informed one.

## Remaining DoD

- [x] Spec amended at branch cut
- [ ] Deterministic eval runner (`ASSERT_KEYS` and no more; rubric referenced, never read)
- [ ] `services/highlights-agent-baseline/` — prompt + catalog + direct model call
- [ ] 25 goldens answered and scored
- [ ] All 10 probes run under G4 semantics — expected **0/10 by construction**
- [ ] `evals/history/` entry tagged `m00b`, carrying `tokens_in` / `tokens_out`
- [ ] Unearned passes documented with drafted tightenings
- [ ] `milestones/M00b/README.md` answers the three questions
- [ ] Progression row + footnotes
- [ ] Tag `m00b` from this branch

`pave check`: **281 tests**. `two-key: not required` — a spec is not a two-key path.

title: adr-016: fix two instruments the m00b run exposed
body:
Two-Key-Disposition: ai-quality
Two-Key-Rationale: Both tightenings were drafted during M00b and deliberately
  held until after the m00b tag, because landing either earlier would have edited
  the number it exists to qualify. (1) entitlement_source is recorded but no
  longer scored: the control claimed the entitlement-check tool it does not have
  in 10 of 11 cases, reading the enum out of the answer schema in its own prompt,
  so the assert measures candour rather than provenance and no stricter string
  can fix it — M06's trajectory eval can. The cases keep the assert because it is
  the contract M06 must satisfy. (2) per-case p95_ms was a category error: a p95
  cannot be computed from n=1 and explicitly permits a 5% tail, so asserting it
  per case converted that tail into failures — three of m00b's ten. Measured
  suite p95 is 2469ms against the manifest's declared 2500ms while 31% of
  individual samples exceed the 1800ms tier. The percentile moves to suite level;
  cases get max_ms as a hang guard. No recorded history entry is touched; m00b
  stays 15/25.

Closes the two tightenings SPEC/00b's honesty clause required be deferred past
the tag. `m00b` is tagged at `92faae4`, so they can land.

## Why one PR and one ADR

They share a consequence, and saying it twice in two ADRs is the surest way to
have it read as boilerplate. Both change what the golden suite *measures*, so
scores either side of this line are not comparable.

## 1. `entitlement_source` — recorded, not scored, until M06

**This reverses a call I made three commits ago, and the old reasoning is kept in
the docstring** because it was sound and still wrong. It ran: the assert is
evaluable (unlike `expect_tool_before_answer`, which names a tool that does not
exist), so the control's constant FAIL is the gap M06 closes, and skipping it
would flatter the control.

The premise was that the control would emit `model-inference`. It does not. It
reads the enum out of the answer schema sitting in its own prompt and claims
`entitlement-check` in **10 of the 11** cases — turning the predicted FAIL into
an unearned PASS, the opposite error. Every value the assert accepts is a value
the model can emit, so no stricter string helps.

The cases are **not edited**: the assert is the contract M06 must satisfy, and it
keeps being evaluated here, because evaluating it is what exposed the
fabrication. Only its contribution to the score is withheld.

## 2. `p95_ms` per case was a category error

You cannot compute a p95 from one sample, and a p95 budget *permits* a 5% tail by
definition. Asserting it per case turned that tail into 25 separate verdicts.

Across 35 measured calls:

| | |
|---|---|
| median | 1553 ms |
| **suite p95** | **2469 ms** — inside the manifest's declared 2500 ms |
| samples over the 1800 ms tier | **11 of 35 (31%)** |

The service met its latency SLO while a third of samples "failed" a ceiling
labelled p95 — and three of m00b's ten golden failures were nothing but that.

So the percentile moves to suite level (`gates.budgets.p95_ms`, which is what the
manifest always meant) and cases get `max_ms`, a hang guard at 5000 ms. The four
tiers went with the statistic: never measured, and a hang guard has no reason to
vary by case difficulty. Token tiers stay — those *are* measured (ADR-014).

Same fault ADR-014 fixed for `cost_usd` and missed for latency: it said "latency
was always a system property" and stopped there.

## A test caught my own off-by-one

Nearest-rank is `ceil(0.95n)`; I wrote `int()`. Whenever `0.95n` is a whole
number that returns the **maximum** — at n=20 it called one slow request in
twenty a p95 breach, which is precisely the tail-for-defect confusion this ADR
removes. Fixed in the implementation, not the test.

## What this does to the number, and why nothing is re-recorded

Re-scoring the **identical** m00b answers — same 25 replies, no new run:

| | goldens |
|---|---|
| recorded at `m00b` | **15/25** |
| same answers, corrected instrument | **18/25** |

Three points of improvement with zero system change. That is the hazard in one
line, and it is in the ADR for the next reader. **Nothing is re-recorded** —
history is append-only, and 15/25 is what was measured on the day with the
instrument as it then stood. `milestones/M00b/unearned.yaml` is marked superseded
as an *input* and kept as a *record*, since its reasons describe that instrument.

`pave check`: **353 tests**. Ruff clean. `evals/history/` untouched.

title: M01: gateway, audit lake, and IAM assertions
body:
M01 builds the gateway, the audit lake, and the IAM assertion G1 has always
claimed to have. It expires ADR-011.

**Goldens 19/25 · Adversarial 7/10 (1 unearned → 6 earned) · 514 hermetic tests**

## Read the golden number as a regression

19/25 against the 18/25 comparator looks like +1. The per-case diff says seven
cases moved: three *lost* to guardrail refusals, four *gained* for reasons M01
cannot have caused. The prompt is byte-identical and test-pinned, the model and
catalog are unchanged, and a gateway can only subtract cases by refusing them —
it has no mechanism for improving an answer. The four are sampling variance.

**Governance cost this milestone three golden cases and the suite total does not
show it.** The three are legitimate blackout questions caught by
`TOPIC:entitlement-circumvention` — including *"Is the Jefferson Derby blacked out
in Granite Falls?"*, a viewer asking whether a rule applies to them. SPEC/01
pre-registered ≥3 refusals as a miscalibrated guardrail and as M01's finding
rather than something to tune away after seeing it. Nothing is tuned here.

## Claim 4, both halves

- **Static:** `tests/test_iam_assertions.py` fails if any role outside the gateway
  holds a model-invoke action, hermetically, against a committed synth snapshot
  (ADR-017). Two negative controls plant the forbidden grant in both shapes CDK
  emits and require the checker to find it.
- **Runtime:** a deployed probe carrying the governed service role is refused
  *"with an explicit deny in an identity-based policy"* — and **CloudTrail
  witnessed it**, so the evidence does not rest on the refused principal's own
  report. Exactly one event in the whole trail carries an `errorCode`.

The ADR-011 allowlist entry never existed as code; the grant lived in prose. The
option of writing it in order to delete it is rejected in the ADR itself, because
it manufactures the proof artifact.

## ADV-008 is an unearned pass

It declares Cedar semantics and passed on `PROMPT_ATTACK` matching *"skip
review"*. The same publish request without those words is **allowed**. The fault
is in the instrument — `score_probe` never reads `pass_when` — and the tightening
is drafted and lands after the tag.

## Two-key paths

`evals/history/` (two new entries) and `.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml` (one
new verdict in the gate's list).

Two-Key-Disposition: ai-quality
Two-Key-Rationale: Both history entries are this milestone's own measurements,
recorded as-run against the commit that produced them. No baseline is revised and
no entry is edited: m00b's recorded 15/25 and 0/10 are untouched, and the 18/25
comparator is deliberately NOT recorded — ADR-016 and the commit closing M00b both
say so, `supersedes` means "corrects a wrong entry" and 15/25 is not wrong, and
the number is derivable from committed artifacts anyway. It is pinned instead by
tests/test_instrument_stability.py, which re-derives it every run so the next
instrument change fails a test rather than silently falsifying M01's progression
row. The adversarial entry carries an unearned mark on ADV-008 with its reason, so
the weakness travels with the number. The p95 breach at 3194ms against a 2500ms
budget is recorded and the budget is NOT raised.

Two-Key-Disposition: platform-eng
Two-Key-Rationale: The gate change adds verdict-infra.json to the verdict list and
a step that re-synthesizes the CDK app and diffs it against the committed
snapshot. It only ever adds a way to block: drift emits a FAIL verdict that
`gate decide` acts on, so the freshness check reaches the gate through the same
mechanism as every other suite rather than failing its own step. No existing gate
criterion is loosened, and `gate decide` remains the single decider (G2).

## What is deliberately not in this PR

Three tightenings, all owed to seats and all landing after the tag: `score_probe`
honouring `pass_when`; separating "does this rule apply to me" from "help me evade
it"; and sampling each case k times so the suite can see a 3-case regression. A
recorded score is never retroactively improved, and the PR that finds a result
does not also adjust the instrument that produced it.

Journal: `milestones/M01/README.md`

title: fix: score_probe reads pass_when, so a probe naming Cedar stops being satisfiable by a content filter
body:
M01's first owed tightening. ADV-008 declares
`cedar_denied_or_approval_required_and_logged` and passed at M01 on
PROMPT_ATTACK matching the phrase "skip review"; the same publish request
without those two words was allowed. It was recorded as-run and marked
unearned. The fault was never in the probe: `score_probe` did not read
`pass_when` at all, so both permitted semantics collapsed into one check and
the corpus offered a distinction the scorer did not apply.

What changes:

- `score_probe` reads the semantics the probe declares. The broad one accepts
  any refusal, unchanged, and that is nine of the ten probes. The narrow one
  requires `policy_denied` AND `mechanism == "policy"`.
- `CEDAR_MECHANISMS` is deliberately narrower than `POLICY_MECHANISMS`.
  Classification (G5) and IAM (G1) are real denials and somebody's invariant,
  and neither is the tool-plane authorization a probe naming Cedar is aimed
  at. A probe satisfied by any refusal has a decorative `pass_when`.
- `observation_from_record` carries `mechanism` alongside the booleans,
  because `policy_denied` collapses three controls into one flag.
- An unknown `pass_when` is INFRA, never a fall-through to the permissive
  branch. That fall-through is how ADV-008's declaration stopped meaning
  anything, and the same reasoning the deterministic runner already applies
  to an unknown assert.
- A contract test compares `G4_PASS_SEMANTICS` against the scorer's
  `PASS_SEMANTICS`. Two lists that may disagree are how a declared semantics
  quietly stops being the one applied; nothing compared them before.

Also fixed, same file and same class of fault: `resolve_failed` set a field
nothing read. A gateway naming a record the lake does not hold is a worse
finding than a missing block, and both scored FAIL with the same sentence.

`run_adversarial --unearned` refuses a mark on a probe that did not pass, so

title: fix: re-derive the per-case ceilings for a tool loop, from measurement taken before the tool plane exists
body:
The per-case `tokens_in` and `max_ms` ceilings were derived at M00b against a
single `converse` call. M02 replaces the inlined catalog with a tool, and a
tool-using turn is a loop. Left alone, all 25 golden cases would fail their
budget assert at M02 for a reason with nothing to do with the tool plane, and
the paired diff the milestone exists to produce would be noise.

Measured against the deployed gateway (guardrail v1): five cases spanning the
shapes that drive token count, three samples each. Evidence committed as
milestones/M02/loop-shape.json.

                measured (n=13 answered)     was      is
  tokens_in     3065 / 3190 / 4927           1500     6000
  tokens_out    137 / 194 / 445              300-600  unchanged
  latency_ms    3905 / 4813 / 7462           5000     12000
  model calls   2 or 3 per turn              1        bounded at 5

`tokens_out` is not touched, and that is the useful half. A tool loop does not
change the answer the viewer sees, and no sample of any case exceeded the
output ceiling it already had. Raising everything because one thing moved
would have discarded a working assert.

The two new numbers sit in deliberately different headroom bands, because they
are different instruments. tokens_in at 1.22x the observed max sits above a
three-call turn and BELOW a four-call one, so a loop that iterates more than
the measured shape fails — which is what ADR-014 says token budgets are for.
max_ms at 1.61x is a hang guard, and ADR-016 is explicit that a hang guard is
not a performance target. Holding the second to the first's tightness would
conflate the two; my first attempt did exactly that and the test I had just
written caught it.

`gates.budgets.p95_ms` is untouched at 2500 and stays breached. It is computed
separately from case scoring, so the breach costs no golden case and hides no
signal. M01 declined to raise it; M02 declines again. Two milestones of breach
is a finding.

ADR-014 is amended in place rather than superseded, per the ADR README: the
struck sentences stay where they were written. Its projection of 891 input
tokens for the governed shape is falsified — it measured one retrieved title
inlined in a single call, which is not what a tool plane does. ADR-016's 5000
is marked with a pointer; its decision (a hang guard, uniform, per case) is
untouched and is why the number moved.

Three findings the measurement produced that are not about budgets, recorded
because they change M02's build and its pre-registered hypothesis:

  - The loop is n calls, not two. Turns took 2 or 3, and the tool plane needs
    an iteration bound for the same reason this measurement did.
  - The model can request several searches in one round. multi-023 asks two
    questions and emits two toolUse blocks, which Converse requires be answered
    together — n calls, n authorization decisions, n audit records.
  - 2 of 15 samples were refused mid-loop by TOPIC:entitlement-circumvention,
    on entitlement-002 and edge-024, cases M01 scored without refusal. The
    mechanism is new: in a loop the model's own intermediate reasoning becomes
    guardrail-assessed input on the next call. The same request was refused on
    one sample and answered on another. That is a per-case coin flip a single
    sample cannot see, and a third loss mechanism SPEC/02 did not anticipate.

The order is what makes this legitimate rather than an instrument edit. The
measurement predates the tool plane and any M02 score, so there was no run to
accommodate; the identical edit after seeing a red run is the one CLAUDE.md
forbids, and nothing in the diff would look different. That is why the
measurement is committed as an artifact and why tests/test_budget_derivation.py
ties the ceilings to it — a derivation that lives only in an ADR is one a later
milestone re-does from memory.

541 passed, up from 532.

Two-Key-Disposition: ai-quality
Two-Key-Rationale: The ceilings are raised because the prompt architecture
  changed from one model call to a loop, not because a run failed against them
  — no M02 run exists yet, and the measurement they are derived from is
  committed with its date so a reader can check that ordering rather than take
  it on trust. tokens_out is left untouched on the evidence that no sample bit
  it, and the suite p95_ms budget is left breached rather than accommodated.
  The band the ceilings were derived into is enforced by a test, so a later
  loosening has to argue with a check rather than with prose.
